source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Carrying fairly little established risk with repeated use into the exact same joint over an extended period of ongoing, long-term treatment","B":"Repeated corticosteroid injections into the same joint may be associated with cartilage damage and other local effects over time, limiting how frequently they should be given","C":"Having fairly little measurable effect on the client's joint pain, despite being given specifically for that exact clinical purpose during the visit","D":"Needing to be given on a daily basis in order to remain clinically effective at managing the client's ongoing joint pain over the long term of their care"}}
source_row.rationale: Intra-articular corticosteroid injection frequency is generally limited because repeated injections into the same joint may be associated with cartilage damage and other local effects over time, so providers typically limit the frequency of these injections for any given joint.
